review_notes: I read the whole file and BlockSubstitution.lean, and searched for uses of the zero/succ lemmas in the library and its tests. I did not run Lean. The simpNF claim below comes from reading the rules, not from running the linter. I considered adding @[simp] to the `_succ` lemmas and decided against it. Both are unfolding or one-step recursion lemmas, and the file and BlockSubstitutionLaws use them only through explicit `rw`/`simp only`. Making them simp would expand iterates unnecessarily. The one clear issue is the redundant simp attribute on `eval_iteratedBlockSubst_zero`.

findings.excerpt:
theorem eval_iteratedBlockSubst_zero (p : MvPolynomial ι R)
    (x : (Fin 0 → ι) → R) : eval x (iteratedBlockSubst p 0) = x Fin.elim0 := by
  simp [iteratedBlockSubst]
findings.problem: The simp attribute on this lemma competes with `iteratedBlockSubst_zero`, which is also @[simp] and rewrites `iteratedBlockSubst p 0` to `X Fin.elim0`. Simp rewrites subterms before the enclosing term. In `eval x (iteratedBlockSubst p 0)` the inner term is therefore rewritten first, and `eval_X` finishes the job. The LHS of this lemma is then never seen in its original form, so the rule is dead. A simpNF-style check would likely flag it as provable by other simp lemmas. Its proof is `simp [iteratedBlockSubst]`, which unfolds the definition rather than citing the existing simp rules. That suggests the attribute carries no weight.
findings.proposed_change: Remove @[simp] from `eval_iteratedBlockSubst_zero`, and keep it as a plain convenience lemma. The proof can use the existing simp set (`by simp`) or `by rw [iteratedBlockSubst_zero, eval_X]`. Keep @[simp] only on `iteratedBlockSubst_zero`, so the simp normal form of the zero iterate is `X Fin.elim0`.
findings.benefit: The simp set has one canonical rule for the zero iterate instead of two overlapping ones. It also avoids a likely simpNF lint failure. A reader no longer has to wonder which rule fires. The users of the lemma (e.g. `simpa only [..., eval_iteratedBlockSubst_zero]` here and `eval_iteratedBlockSubst_zero p x` in the tests) refer to it by name, so they are unaffected.

evidence.excerpt:
@[simp]
theorem iteratedBlockSubst_zero (p : MvPolynomial ι R) :
    iteratedBlockSubst p 0 = X Fin.elim0 := rfl
